content.title: About
content.content: Singapore Sling is a classic cocktail created in 1915 by bartender Harry Wong (often credited to Ngiam Tong Boon) at the Raffles Hotel in Singapore. It blends gin, cherry brandy, vermouth, blackcurrant liqueur, pineapple juice, lime juice, grenadine and bitters, delivering a bright fruity flavor with a subtle bitter edge.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The original recipe contained only gin, cherry brandy and vermouth; the other ingredients were added later.
The drink gained worldwide fame after appearing in the 1988 film “Cocktail”.
It is traditionally served in a tall glass over ice, garnished with a cherry, a pineapple wedge and a sprig of mint.
Many variations exist, but the “Raffles” version is considered the canonical recipe.
In 2015, to celebrate the cocktail’s centenary, the Raffles Hotel opened a dedicated Singapore Sling Bar.

items.title: Vitamin C from pineapple and lime juice
items.content: The juices provide vitamin C, which supports the immune system and acts as an antioxidant.

items.title: Antioxidants from cherry brandy and grenadine
items.content: Fruit liqueurs contain polyphenols that help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Moderate consumption may promote relaxation
items.content: Alcohol in moderate amounts can reduce stress and improve mood.

items.title: Alcohol
items.content: Excessive alcohol intake can lead to health problems, dependence, and increased injury risk.

items.title: Sugar
items.content: The cocktail is high in sugar from grenadine and fruit juices, which may be an issue for people with diabetes or weight concerns.

items.title: Allergy to ingredients
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to pineapple, citrus, or other components.

content.title: How to Drink
content.content: Serve Singapore Sling in a tall glass over ice, garnish with a cherry, a pineapple slice and a mint sprig. Sip slowly to appreciate its complex aroma and flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store opened juices and liqueurs in the refrigerator. Mixed cocktail is best enjoyed immediately, as melting ice dilutes the drink and alters its taste.
